texts: I need a doha about the true saint, whose tongue speaks truth though he was born in a humble hut and not a palace, and about how the wise ask for his wisdom and not his family or his caste
tongue, palace, true saint
Do not ask the saint his caste; ask what his tongue has learned, for wisdom outshines the palace of his birth
the holy man in our lane was born poor and has no family name, yet his tongue has comforted three generations while the palace-born scholars only lecture
doha on judging a saint by his words, not his birth, tongue and palace
Ask not in whose house the saint was born; ask what house of wisdom he has built within
saint, house, wisdom
doha on not asking a saint's caste, just see his wisdom, house and all
my aunt would never ask the saint who came to our house which family he belonged to; she only asked what he had understood about life
Can you shape a verse about the saint whose family house nobody knows, whose caste and birth no one asks, because the wise value what he has learned and what he gives and not where he came from
Ask the saint for his wisdom, not his birth; the stream has no caste, and neither does the sage
dont ask a saint his caste, ask what he knows
my grandfather sat with a wandering holy man for hours and only asked what he had learned in life, never once where he was from
true saint, wisdom
I want a doha about the true saint whose worth is in his wisdom and not in his family, a lesson for those who ask a holy man his caste before they ask him what he has understood of life
doha on sadhus who have real wisdom, not just caste or rank
an elderly man from a low-born family became the most respected teacher in our village because of what he knew and how he lived
The holy man is known by what he gives, not by whom he was born to; ask his wisdom, and leave his name
Write a doha about how a true saint should be measured by his wisdom and conduct and not by his birth, and how foolish it is to turn away a wise man because of his caste
saint's wisdom, not birth
the saint everyone respects in our town was born to an oil press family and worked a furnace for years before he took to the road, and now kings seek his advice

Give me a doha on a saint born to the humble family of an oil press worker, who passed through the furnace of hardship and emerged with wisdom, honoured by those who look at his worth and not his birth
furnace, oil press, true saint
The furnace tests the metal and the oil press the grain; the true saint is tested by life and shines
doha on a saint tested in a furnace, oil press too
my uncle, who makes winnowing fans, was taught by a holy man on the mountain who never asked his family name, only whether he was ready to learn
winnowing fan, mountain, saint
doha on a saint, a winnowing fan & a mountain, wisdom before caste
The winnowing fan sifts grain from husk, and the wise sift the saint's wisdom from his birth, as the mountain stands apart from the pebbles

I need a doha about the winnowing fan that sifts grain from husk and the people who must sift a saint's wisdom from the question of his caste, for the wise man lives on a mountain above such questions
a wandering monk said one thing to me that went through me like an arrow, and I never even thought to ask who his family was
The saint's word darts like an arrow to the heart; who asks the archer's caste before it lands
Write a doha about the saint whose words are straight as an arrow and strike the target of the heart, and how foolish it is to ask the archer his birth when the arrow has found its mark
saint, arrow, wisdom
doha on a saint whose words are like an arrow, not caste
a holy man who spun at a spinning wheel in our village was fearless as a lion before the rich, and nobody thought of asking his caste
doha on a saint like a lion at a spinning wheel, caste doesnt matter
Looking for a doha about the true saint, brave as a lion and humble as the spinning wheel, who is honoured for his wisdom by the wise, and whose caste or family no one cares to ask about
lion, spinning wheel, saint
The lion needs no pedigree, the spinning wheel no title; the saint is known by what he is
rainbird, true saint
The rainbird asks for only the rain, and the wise ask for only the saint's wisdom, never his name or his birth
doha on a saint like the rainbird, ask his wisdom not his caste
Give me a doha on the seeker who waits for the saint's wisdom as the rainbird waits for rain, with no concern for the saint's caste or family, because only the teaching can quench the thirst
my uncle waited three days for a rainbird-like holy man to speak and then never asked his caste, only what the man meant by his words
saint's wisdom matters
I want a doha about the true holy man, whose value lies in what he has realised and teaches, and how shallow it is to ask his caste and clan when we should ask for his wisdom
my father was told by his elders to avoid a wise old man because of his low caste, but he went anyway and learned more from him than from any of them
When the saint speaks truth, who asks his birth? Ask what he knows, and let the rest fall silent
doha pls, dont ask the sadhu his caste
doha on saints being like a swan and a heron, ask for wisdom not caste
I saw both a swan and a heron by the pond and my grandfather said that is how you tell a real holy man from a fake one, by what he does and not what he looks like

Write a doha about the true saint who is like a swan, discerning, and the false one like a heron, standing still, and how the wise judge them not by their caste or their appearance but by their wisdom
swan, heron, true saint
The heron stands in the water and the swan swims in it, but the swan knows the cream; ask the saint's wisdom, not his looks

Can you shape a verse about a saint who lives in plain cotton clothes and works at the grindstone for his bread, whose wisdom shines far beyond the question of his caste, which only fools bother to ask
the old holy man in cotton clothes who grinds flour at the grindstone in our village is the wisest person I know, and no one asks his caste
He wears plain cotton and turns the grindstone, and his wisdom outshines the robes of all the high-born
cotton, grindstone, saint
doha on a saint with cotton robes and a grindstone life
doha on a saint in the forest, dont ask caste ask wisdom
a hermit in the forest near our village was visited by people of every caste, and none of them thought to ask where he was born
forest saint, wisdom
Looking for a doha about the saint who lives in the forest, whose caste and clan no one knows, and who is honoured only for the clarity of his understanding and the peace in his eyes
The forest asks not the caste of those who shelter in it, nor the wise the birth of the saint who walks there
doha on judging a sadhu by his wisdom
The mind of the saint is his true family; ask about it, and forget all else
Write a doha about the folly of judging a holy man by his family, caste and clothes, when the only fair test is what he has understood and can teach to the seekers who come to him
true saint, true wisdom
a friend of mine refused to take advice from a wise elder because of his background, and he lost a great chance to learn
a holy man stood at the crossroads in our village and told everyone which road led where, and nobody cared what his caste was
I need a doha about the true saint who stands at the crossroads and shows wanderers the right way, and how the wise follow him without asking his caste, since the direction is what matters
At the crossroads the saint points the way, and nobody asks his caste before following
crossroads, saint, wisdom
doha on a saint at the crossroads, wisdom over caste
moneylender, saint, wisdom
doha on a moneylender vs a saint, ask wisdom not wealth or caste
The moneylender counts his wealth, the saint counts his wisdom; ask of the saint what he knows, not whence he came
Can you shape a verse about a moneylender who values everything by price and a true saint valued by his wisdom, and the wise person who asks the saint what he knows and not what family he comes from
the moneylender in our lane judges everyone by wealth and caste, but the old holy man who sits outside his place is the one everybody consults about life
jaggery, saint's wisdom
Write a doha about jaggery that is sweet no matter whose hands made it and about the saint whose wisdom is sweet whatever his caste, for the wise take the sweetness and do not ask the maker's lineage
my grandmother ate jaggery from a low-caste woman's hand and said the saint's wisdom, too, is sweet no matter whose lips it comes from
Jaggery is sweet whatever hands it comes from; so the saint's wisdom, whatever his birth
doha on a saint and jaggery, sweet wisdom doesnt care for caste
a moneylender and a moth-eaten old holy man lived next to each other in our village, and in the end everyone sought the second one for advice
Give me a doha on the moneylender who chases wealth like a moth chases a glow, and the saint who is wise and content, to whom the wise go for guidance without asking about his caste
The moth dies for a glimmer and the moneylender for his coins; the saint lives on, and his birth is no one's concern
moneylender, moth, saint
doha on a saint, a moth and a moneylender, wisdom not caste
The lotus doesn't ask what mud it grew in and the lamp doesn't ask whom it lights; so the saint
lotus, lamp, saint
I need a doha about the saint who is a lotus rising from any mud and a lamp lighting any home, and about how the wise ask only what he knows and never what his caste or birth might be
doha on a saint, lotus and lamp, ask his light not his caste
the saint who lit a lamp in front of a lotus pond every evening was born in a family nobody respected, yet the whole district respected him
my professor, who came from the lowest rung of society, became the most respected scholar in our city purely through his learning
doha pls on a sadhu being judged by knowledge not caste
saint's worth
Before the true saint all births are equal, and all that remains is what he has become
Write a doha about a saint whose worth cannot be measured by his caste, his birth or his clothes, but only by the depth of his understanding and the kindness with which he shares it with the seeker
The forehead mark does not make the saint; the bee does not ask the flower's caste before drinking honey
doha on a saint with a forehead mark and a bee, wisdom is what counts

Looking for a doha about the saint who wears no grand forehead mark, and about the seeker who takes his wisdom like a bee takes honey from a flower, without asking the flower's caste or the saint's birth
a holy man with a plain forehead mark and a bee on his shoulder was always smiling, and no one asked his caste before taking his advice
forehead mark, bee, saint
The fish does not ask the water's caste, nor the wise the saint's; wisdom is the only water they seek
doha on a saint and a fish, ask wisdom not caste
Give me a doha on the seeker who goes to the saint as a fish goes to water, without asking about its caste or its source
a fisherman's son who caught fish in the lake became the wisest teacher in our region, and people from every caste went to him without asking about his family
fish, saint
crossroads, cotton, saint
doha on a saint at the crossroads, cotton clothes, ask wisdom
Compose a doha about the holy man in plain cotton at the crossroads, who gives the right directions to every passer-by, and who is honoured not for his caste but for the clarity of his teaching
an old man in rough cotton at the crossroads gave me better advice about my life than any professor, and I never asked who his people were
At the crossroads, in plain cotton, sits the saint; the wise ask him the way and forget to ask his caste
doha on a saint, a rope & wisdom over caste
Can you shape a verse about the saint who throws a rope of wisdom to those who are sinking, and about how the wise take hold without asking the saint's caste or family
when the stream flooded, a low-born holy man threw us a rope, and nobody in the village thought of his caste when they held on
rope, saint, wisdom
The saint's wisdom is a rope thrown to the drowning, and nobody asks the thrower's caste before holding on
The moth does not ask the glow its name; the seeker should not ask the saint his birth
doha on a saint and a moth, ask wisdom not caste
moth, saint, wisdom
Looking for a doha about the seeker who rushes toward the saint like a moth toward a glow, without questions about caste or family, because wisdom is what draws him and nothing else
a moth fluttered round the holy man as he spoke to the crowd, and no one in that crowd thought to ask about his caste
Write a doha about the saint who churns the cream of experience into the butter of wisdom, and how the wise partake without asking about his caste or clan, since the butter is the same
The churn brings out the butter whoever turns it; so wisdom, whatever the saint's birth
churn, saint, wisdom
my aunt churns butter every morning and says wisdom is like that, whoever works for it gets it, and the saint's caste has no bearing on it
doha on a saint working a churn, caste is irrelevant
doha on a saint who is gold, ask his worth not caste
my father said that a low-born holy man he once met was worth more than any gold, and that he regretted not asking more questions
I need a doha about the saint who is like pure gold, whose worth is the same whatever family or caste he comes from, and about the foolish who judge gold by the pouch in which it lies
Gold is gold whatever hands have held it; so the saint, whose worth does not depend on his birth
gold, saint's worth
doha on not asking a saint's caste
ask wisdom, not caste
I'd like a doha about how a true saint answers every question about his caste with a question about the seeker's own life, since the real matter is wisdom and the way a man lives and not his family
when my neighbour's son asked a wandering sage which caste he belonged to, the sage smiled and asked him what he wanted to learn
Ask the saint what he has seen, not what his father was; the seeker who does this goes home full
a snake slid past the holy man as he talked to us, and he did not move, and none of us asked about his caste, only how he had learned such calm
Can you shape a verse about a saint who sits unafraid beside a snake, and about the people who come to him for his calm and his wisdom
The snake bites the foolish and spares the wise, and the wise recognise the saint without asking his birth
snake, saint's wisdom
doha on a saint and a snake, wisdom beyond caste
recognising a true saint
The true saint can be known not by his family but by his peace, and the false by his pride
my grandmother says you can tell a real holy man by the calm he brings into a room, not by anything about his birth or clothes
Write a doha about how to recognise a saint, not by his caste or dress or following, but by his wisdom, calm and kindness to all who come before him, rich or poor
doha on a real saint vs a fake one
doha on a sadhu's real value
when the village elder died, the people who wept loudest were the lowest caste, because he had been the only one to treat them as equals
saint's real worth
Give me a doha on the true saint, who needs no pedigree to be honoured, who is recognised by the people he has helped and the wisdom he has shared, greater than the high-born who merely have a name
His birth is a few lines in a ledger, but his wisdom is written in every heart that has met him
doha on a saint who is wise and humble
I need a doha about the humble saint whose birth is unknown or lowly, yet who is honoured by the learned because of his wisdom, and who never asks for the respect that people freely give him
a monk at our school was born of a lowly family, yet the principal himself stood up when he entered a room
humble wise saint
The saint seeks no seat of honour; the seat of honour seeks the saint, whatever his birth
the old man outside the mosque was tested by everyone with questions, as a jeweller tests with a touchstone, and he passed every test, though nobody asked his caste
doha on a saint at the mosque, test his wisdom on a touchstone

Write a doha about the saint who sits in the mosque courtyard and is tested on the touchstone of deeds and wisdom, and how the wise do not ask about his family or community but about what he has realised
At the mosque or beyond it, test the saint on the touchstone of his deeds, and do not ask his clan
mosque, touchstone, saint
doha on a saint with a spinning wheel & one-string lute
a wandering singer with a one-string lute and a spinning wheel on his cart came to our village, and his songs were wiser than any sermon, though no one asked his caste
Looking for a doha about the saint who spins at his spinning wheel by day and plays a one-string lute by night, whose song is full of wisdom
With a spinning wheel and a one-string lute he sings, and who is to ask his caste when the song is true
spinning wheel, one-string lute, saint
wisdom over birth
The saint's learning is his only family, and it is a large one that welcomes all
I want a doha about the foolishness of asking a holy man his caste and background before listening to him, when his learning and his conduct are all that matter in the eyes of those who truly seek
doha on a saint's wisdom being worth more than his birth
my mother refused to ask the doctor who saved her life about his caste, saying it did not matter and was irrelevant to his skill
Give me a doha on the saint who plants a seed of wisdom in the hearts of those who come, and how the wise let it grow without asking about his caste or lineage, since the seed carries no name
doha on a saint's wisdom like a seed, caste doesnt matter
a holy man dropped one idea in my mind like a seed, and it grew into my whole outlook, and I never even asked who he was
A seed does not ask whose hand sowed it; so wisdom grows, whoever the saint who plants it
seed, saint's wisdom
doha on respecting a sadhu for what he knows
Write a doha about how true respect for a saint should come from his wisdom and character and not from any inherited rank or caste, because only what a man has made of himself is truly his
wisdom, not lineage
Bow to the saint for his wisdom, not his lineage; the lineage is borrowed, the wisdom his own
my elders told me to ignore a clever young monk because of his background, but I listened to him and I am glad
doha on a saint, a thief and a boat, wisdom not caste
a former thief, now a boatman and holy man, ferried us across in his boat and gave us the best advice of our lives, and nobody asked what his caste was
Can you shape a verse about a saint and a thief who share a boat on the water, and how the saint's wisdom reaches even the thief, while nobody aboard asks the saint about his caste or birth
thief, boat, saint
The boat carries thief and saint alike, but the saint carries the thief across to wisdom, whatever his birth
Looking for a doha about the true saint who shares what he knows freely with all, and about the wisdom of those who ask him what he understands and not what caste or community he belongs to
the man who taught my father to read was thought a low person by the village, yet everyone ended up consulting him
doha on the real saint
He who shares his wisdom freely is a saint, whatever the family into which he was born
a true saint
our village moneylender asks people their caste before he lends, but the old grindstone-man who is also a saint gives wisdom to anyone who comes
doha on a saint, a grindstone and a moneylender
Write a doha about the saint who works at a grindstone for his bread and gives wisdom free, while the moneylender nearby squeezes the poor, and the wise ask the saint what he knows, not his caste
grindstone, moneylender, saint
The grindstone grinds, the moneylender squeezes, and the saint gives; ask not the saint's caste but his gift
I need a doha about a saint who sits under the stars while a fly rests on his shoulder, both of them accepted by the night, and about how the wise seeker asks only for the saint's teaching
doha on a saint under the stars with a fly, ask his wisdom
we slept in the open under the stars, with a fly bothering us, and an old holy man spoke to us until dawn, and none of us asked where he was from
Under the stars a fly settles on the saint's shoulder, and neither asks the other's caste
stars, fly, saint
peacock, bridge, saint
doha on a saint, a peacock and a bridge, wisdom over caste
a holy man lived near the old bridge where peacocks gathered, and people of every caste crossed it just to hear him speak
The peacock dances for all and the bridge carries all; so the saint, whose wisdom does not ask your caste
Can you shape a verse about a saint who lives by a bridge where a peacock dances every evening, and the people who cross to meet him and ask him only about the truth, never about his family or caste
saint of wisdom
The saint's caste is silence, his clan is kindness; ask nothing else of him
Write a doha about how a true saint is known by his wisdom and compassion and not by the caste or position of his family, and how the wise approach him with questions about life and not about birth
doha on a saint known by wisdom not caste
when I was sick, a stranger who looked after me turned out to be from the lowest caste, and he taught me what holiness really is
an old man sat under a tree by the village well advising people of every caste, and the village learned to ask him about life and not his family
Under the tree, beside the well, the saint gives all, and no one asks the caste of his giving
doha on a saint under a tree by a well, ask wisdom
tree, well, saint
Give me a doha on the saint who sits under a tree beside the well where people of every caste draw water, and who gives his wisdom to all of them equally, without a single question about birth
rope, bitter gourd, saint
doha on a saint, rope and bitter gourd, ask wisdom not caste
the holy man's advice was bitter as a bitter gourd, but he pulled me up like a rope when I fell, and I never asked who his people were
The rope holds the bucket, the bitter gourd cures the blood, and the saint's rough word heals; ask not his caste
I need a doha about the saint whose words are as bitter as a bitter gourd but as helpful as a rope to the drowning, and about how the wise take his teaching without asking about his birth or caste
doha on a saint at the crossroads, wisdom over caste
Let every crossroads lead to the saint, and let none ask whose son he is
crossroads, saint
an old holy man at the crossroads outside our town is visited by people of every kind, and not one of them asks about his family
Compose a doha about the saint at the crossroads whom all roads meet, rich and poor, high and low, and about how none of those who come to him ask about his caste but only about the way

I want a doha about how people should approach a saint with questions about truth and not caste, and how the wise teacher gives his light to anyone who comes with an honest heart, whatever their own background
my grandmother told me that her best teacher was a woman nobody respected, and she regretted every year that she had not honoured her earlier
ask his wisdom
doha pls on a saint's wisdom over his birth
Ask not the saint his father's name; ask what the Lord has taught him in silence
rainbird, door, saint
a rainbird sang by the door of the old holy man's hut as the crowd waited to hear him, and nobody asked what caste he had been born into
doha on a saint, a rainbird and a door, ask wisdom not caste
The rainbird waits at the saint's door, and the seeker beside it, asking nothing of his birth
Looking for a doha about the seeker who waits like the rainbird at the saint's door for a drop of wisdom, who does not ask about the family or caste of the saint
Give me a doha on a saint who works at a spinning wheel and is tested on the touchstone of conduct, and how the wise judge him by what he does and says and not by his family or caste
spinning wheel, touchstone, saint
doha on a saint with a spinning wheel and a touchstone
The spinning wheel turns the plain yarn and the touchstone tests the metal; the saint is tested by deeds, not birth
a holy man who spun at a spinning wheel was tested by the villagers on a touchstone of questions, and he passed, and then no one cared about his caste
my teacher, born of the poorest family in the district, taught three generations of doctors, and the district honours him as a saint
doha on the worth of a saint
worth of a saint

Write a doha about the worth of the true saint, whose knowing and kindness are his only wealth, and about how the wise approach him with respect and ask about his understanding and never about his caste
The saint's worth is in his knowing and his kindness; his birth is a small part of the story
